preset.assumptions: Attenuation: Table I.1 link values, linear between bands. Dispersion: three-term curve fitted through Table I.1 D1550 and S1550 (lambda0 1307.6 nm, S0 0.0889). Not a specific fiber.

numerical_validation.label: simulated (small-signal tone through dispersive_field) against analytical
numerical_validation.method: Intensity-modulation response of a DSB tone, first null by scan; theory f = sqrt(c / (2 lambda^2 |D| L)).

assumptions: Single polarization, no PMD, no nonlinearity, no amplifier or laser noise (link.py).
Attenuation limits are for cable; Table 2 Note 1 excludes short cables such as jumpers.

Table I.1 typical link values are not cable limits. Table I.1 is titled 'Representative values of concatenated optical fibre links', and Appendix I says link attenuation is affected by splices, passive components and installation, which G.652 does not specify. That 0.5 dB/km at 1310 nm exceeds the 0.40 dB/km cable limit for that reason is an inference, not a statement of the Recommendation.
Excess loss added to a Table I.1 link value may count splice and connector loss twice; here it is a sweep parameter that places the error rate in a measurable range, not a splice budget.
Responsivity, V_pi and the modulator are the same at 1550 nm and 1310 nm. Real devices differ between the bands, so the two wavelengths differ here only in the fiber.
The representative dispersion curve is a three-term fit through Table I.1 D and S at 1550 nm, a model choice and not a stated value.
Southampton's fiber type and length are unconfirmed.
